look/keep: A plain decoder only sees the encoder's final state. Attention keeps all of them: one state per input word, here for je, suis, and étudiant. Call them h j, with j counting the input words from zero.
look/score: At each step, the decoder scores every encoder state against its own state, q. A simple score is the dot product, s j equals q dot h j: two, zero, and one.
look/weights: Softmax turns the scores into the attention weights, written alpha j: positive, and adding up to one. Here they are zero point six seven, zero point zero nine, and zero point two four.
mix/context: The context vector is the weighted sum of the states, the sum over j of alpha j times h j: scale each state by its weight, then add them up.
mix/scale: Je's state, two and zero, times zero point six seven, is one point three four and zero. Suis gives zero and zero point zero nine; étudiant, zero point two four and zero.
mix/add: Add them entry by entry: one point three four plus zero point two four is one point five eight, and the second entries give zero point zero nine. Mostly je, a little of the rest.
mix/use: The decoder reads this context along with its own state to predict the next word: I.
every/again: At the next step the decoder's state has moved on, so the scores change, and it looks somewhere else: for am and a, at suis; for student, at étudiant.
every/grid: Stack the weights, one row per output word, and they show which input words each output word drew on.
every/free: Nothing has to squeeze through one fixed-size vector any more: every step can read every input state directly. That is attention.
